title: Write 20 reply templates for the questions support gets most, by Fri 27 Nov
description: When a new organiser writes in, a slow or vague reply loses them. Work under this goal: collect the 20 questions that real users ask most (from support messages the team shares, public posts and the help-centre goals), and write one short, friendly reply template for each with the exact steps checked in the live app and a link to the matching help article if one exists. Each template says who to hand over to when the answer needs a person. No invented customers, no claims the team has not confirmed. Separate from the help centre itself, which holds the long answers. Done when 20 templates are delivered with the question source and a check date for each, and approved by the team.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Group real support questions, then verify and route each reply
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Collect questions only from support material the team shares, public posts and the related help-centre work. For each reply, check the steps in the live app, link the matching help article if available, and add a clear hand-off route for anything that needs a person. Flag missing product answers rather than guessing, and include a check date so replies can be rechecked after changes.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Start from the approved 20-question evidence list and help-answer template, so replies and help answers match
acceptedWorkstreams.description:
Two approved pieces in this project already do much of the groundwork. Reusing them avoids repeating the work and keeps support replies consistent with the help centre:
- 'Collect the 20 questions new organisers ask most, with evidence' (approved) ranks 20 areas by how many different people hit them across 711 Ziki issues. Its notes say no support messages were shared yet.
- 'Write the help-answer template and the order for the first five answers' (approved) sets exact labels, a 'what you'll see' line and a 'Next' link per answer.
Tasks, each finishable:
1. Question list (research): take the 20 from the approved evidence list, then ask the team for a sample of real support messages and re-rank by them if any are shared, so the goal's 'questions real users ask' is met. Record the source for each question.
2. Reply templates (content): 20 short replies (under 120 words each) that answer in two or three steps using the same exact labels as the help answers, link the matching help answer, and name who to hand over to. Placeholders mark anything the team must confirm.
3. Consistency check (content): a table showing each reply, its help answer and its check date, flagging any reply whose steps differ from the help answer.

upvotes.reason: Specific deliverable with a clear scope and a measurable outcome for this goal.

pendingIdeas.title: Cover the questions that arrive from outside support email: app-store reviews, community posts and DMs
pendingIdeas.description: Questions do not only arrive in the support inbox, and the public ones are read by buyers. Work: collect the recurring questions from the app-store review replies, the community workspace and public posts, and mark which of the twenty they duplicate and which are new. Deliver the extra templates for the genuinely new ones, the tone difference for a public answer, and the note on which public question is better answered by fixing the listing than by replying.

upvotes.reason: Public questions from app-store reviews and community posts are read by buyers and are missed by inbox-only templates.

pendingIdeas.title: Quote the button labels exactly as the app shows them, because a near-miss instruction creates the next ticket
pendingIdeas.description: A template that says "open Settings" when the product says "Preferences" reads as written by someone who has never used it, and the user replies to ask. Work: for each reply, walk the steps in the live app, copy the labels verbatim, and note the screen the user should be on when they start. Deliver the templates with a label column checked against the current build, and a list of the labels that changed recently, since those are the ones support still has wrong.

upvotes.reason: Verbatim button labels checked against the live app is exactly what stops a reply creating the next ticket.

pendingIdeas.title: Route by role and channel rather than by name, so a template does not rot when a person leaves
pendingIdeas.description: Handover lines become wrong the week someone changes job, and a wrong handover is worse than none. Work: replace names with roles and the actual intake route (an address, a form, an in-app path), and state what the user should expect after the handover (a reply, a ticket number, nothing). Deliver the handover table by question type, the wording, and the two questions where a handover currently has no owner at all.

upvotes.reason: Role-and-route handovers survive staff changes; names do not.

pendingIdeas.title: Write the "this should not need a reply" list: questions the product should answer on screen instead
pendingIdeas.description: Half the most-asked questions are evidence of a missing label, not a missing answer. Work: from the twenty questions, mark the ones the interface could answer where the confusion happens (what a limit means, who can invite, what happens at term end), and specify the line of copy and its placement. Deliver the split list with a template or a product fix assigned to each, and the three fixes that would remove the most repeat contact.

upvotes.reason: Splitting questions into 'reply' versus 'fix the screen' is the higher-leverage outcome.

pendingIdeas.title: Write the three replies support cannot send alone: refund, data deletion and a security report
pendingIdeas.description: These arrive rarely and matter most, and a wrong first reply creates a legal problem. Work: for each, write what support may say immediately (acknowledge, set a timeline, do not admit or deny), who owns the decision, and which facts must be collected before anything is promised. Deliver the three templates with their approval needs, and the gap list of anything the team has not yet decided, since those decisions are the real deliverable here.

upvotes.reason: Refund, deletion and security replies need escalation rules and no promises; this is the highest-risk support gap.
